L122: ## About This Game
L123: 
L124: This is the original version of Braid from 2009, which may not work well on newer systems. For an updated version of the game with nicer graphics, more levels and a large amount of developer commentary, see Braid, Anniversary Edition.
L125: Braid is a puzzle-platformer, drawn in a painterly style, where you can manipulate the flow of time in strange and unusual ways. From a house in the city, journey to a series of worlds and solve puzzles to rescue an abducted princess. In each world, you have a different power to affect the way time behaves, and it is time's strangeness that creates the puzzles.
L126: The time behaviors include: the ability to rewind, objects that are immune to being rewound, time that is tied to space, parallel realities, time dilation, and perhaps more.
L127: Braid treats your time and attention as precious; there is no filler in this game. Every puzzle shows you something new and interesting about the game world.
L128: 
L129: Key features:
L130: 
L131:   * Newly added Steam Cloud support
L132: Save your in-progress game to the cloud, then play where you left off from on any Steam connected computer.
L133:   * Forgiving yet challenging gameplay:
L134: Braid is a 2-D platform game where you can never die and never lose. Despite this, Braid is challenging — but the challenge is about solving puzzles, rather than forcing you to replay tricky jumps.
L135:   * Rich puzzle environment:
L136: Travel through a series of worlds searching for puzzle pieces, then solving puzzles by manipulating time: rewinding, creating parallel universes, setting up pockets of dilated time. The gameplay feels fresh and new; the puzzles are meant to inspire new ways of thinking.
L137: 
L138:   * Aesthetic design:
L139: A painterly art style and lush, organic soundtrack complement the unique gameplay.
L140:   * Nonlinear story:
L141: A nonlinear fiction links the various worlds and provides real-world metaphors for your time manipulations; in turn, your time manipulations are projections of the real-world themes into playful "what-if" universes where consequences can be explored.
L142: 
L143:   * Nonlinear gameplay:
L144: The game doesn't force you to solve puzzles in order to proceed. If you can't figure something out, just play onward and return to that puzzle later.
